Implemented step 0 of the order gateway: added FixConstants holding SOH = 0x01, EQUALS = '='. tag numbers: 8, 9, 10, 35, 11, 38, 41, 44, 54, 55. msg-type bytes: 'D', 'F'. the single configured instrument symbol for the book

Implemented step 1 of the order gateway:parseLong(byte[] buf, int start, int end). Goal: pure byte-range to long. Foundation for every numeric parse downstream. Walk bytes [start, end). For each: digit = b - '0', reject if outside 0..9, accumulate val = val * 10 + digit.As well as some unit tests

Add parsePrice for FIX price fields (Step 2)
Parse a byte-range FIX price to long cents, reusing parseLong for the integer and fractional parts. Scale the fraction by digit length, not value: one digit *10, two digits as-is.
Reject (-1L sentinel, consistent with parseLong) on: empty range, empty integer part, more than two decimals, non-digit bytes, and non-positive result. The zero/negative price policy is applied here via the > 0 check, since parseLong deliberately treats "0" as a valid parse.
PRICE_SCALE and MAX_DECIMALS kept private to the parser (no second caller). No String/split/BigDecimal; pure byte[] in, off the hot path.
Tested: integer-only, one/two decimals, leading zeros, zero-integer-part with positive fraction, and rejects for >2 decimals, zero, negative, bare dot, empty integer part, trailing dot, trailing junk, and multiple dots. Tests embed each price in a wider buffer to verify offset/length bounds.

Add zero-allocation FIX message scanner (Step 3)
- Add MAX_FIELDS = 32 constant to FixConstants to bound scanner arrays - Add parallel arrays (tags, valStarts, valEnds) to FixParser for allocation-free tokenisation; reuse across messages with no reset needed - Implement FixParser.scan(): tokenises a raw FIX byte buffer into (tag, valueStart, valueEnd) triples; returns field count or -1 on any structural reject (missing '=', unterminated value, non-digit tag, field overflow)

test(gateway): add FixParser tag scanner tests
Cover the Step 3 scanner: session tags pass through in order, '='-in-value delimited by SOH, empty/non-numeric tag and missing '=' rejects, empty value accepted (deferred to Step 5), MAX_FIELDS boundary both sides, and offset/length handling within a larger buffer.

Add checksum validation for FIX messages (Step 4)
Verify tag 10 before any message interpretation: sum every byte up to and including the SOH preceding "10=", mod 256, and compare against the field's three-digit value. Operates on raw byte[] so structural trust is established before the tag scan, independent of the Step 3 scanner arrays.
Locate the trailer by computing from the end (a complete message ends in the 7-byte 10=xxx<SOH>) rather than scanning for it, leaning on the frame decoder's trailer invariant instead of duplicating a scan. Read the three digits via parseLong, which gives free rejection of a malformed checksum field: its -1L sentinel can't equal a 0..255 sum, consistent with the parseLong/parsePrice reject convention.
Guard length < 8 (no room for a summed byte plus the trailer) before indexing. The per-byte & 0xFF is kept for clarity but is not load-bearing: the final & 0xFF already collapses the signed/unsigned difference, since a high byte differs by exactly 256, i.e. 0 mod 256.
Static, pure byte[] in; no String, no io.netty, no com.lmax. Runs at the gateway boundary, off the hot path.
Tested: known-good message (independently computed checksum), corrupted body byte, wrong checksum value, non-digit checksum field, too-short buffer, and the good message embedded in a wider buffer to verify offset/length bounds.

feat(publisher): WebSocket fan-out publisher for execution and book-snapshot events (P4-6)
Add WebSocketPublisher as the outbound edge to React clients, bridging the two Disruptor consumer threads to the Netty ChannelGroup.
- WebSocketPublisher: two stored EventHandler fields (executionHandler / snapshotHandler) allocated once at construction via method-reference, never per message. onExecution emits EXEC frames; onSnapshot emits BOOK frames. Skips serialization entirely when the group is empty. - Serialization: integer cents only — price formatting is React's job (§4). EXEC carries execType name + all carrier fields. BOOK serializes ONLY the [0, levelCount) valid prefix of each side; poisoned array tails never reach the wire (count-authoritative reuse contract). - Slot discipline: each onEvent builds a fresh JSON String fully inside the call before the slot can advance; the mutable carrier is never retained. Fan-out via ChannelGroup is safe from the consumer thread — Netty marshals each write to the channel's own event loop. - ObjectMapper is thread-safe; the two handlers run on different Disruptor consumer threads with no shared mutable serialization scratch. - Tests (WebSocketPublisherTest): EXEC field mapping, NA=-1 sentinel, BOOK valid-prefix-only with poisoned tails, empty-book, one-sided book, ChannelGroup write path, two-channel fan-out with unique EmbeddedChannelId, empty-group skip, and slot-discipline (mutate slot after dispatch). All green.

P4-7: Main bring-up — full pipeline assembled and running
Rewrite Main as the real bootstrap, wiring the complete path from WebSocket client to matching engine and back out to all subscribers (SRS §7, guide P4-7).
Wiring order, which is load-bearing:
MatchingEngine -> OutboundPipeline + SnapshotPipeline (construct) -> MatchingEngineHandler(engine, execRing, snapshotRing) -> engine.setExecutionListener(handler) -> InboundPipeline(handler) -> OrderGateway(inboundRing) -> WebSocketServer(port, gateway) // owns the ChannelGroup -> WebSocketPublisher(server.getChannelGroup()) -> register EXEC/BOOK roles + TradeLogger + MarketDataService -> start outbound, snapshot, inbound, server
The construction graph is circular on paper: the publisher needs the ChannelGroup, which the server owns; the server needs the gateway; the gateway needs the inbound ring; and InboundPipeline attaches its consumer at construction, so the handler must pre-exist the pipeline. Resolved by building the server before the publisher — the group exists at construction, before start() — and registering outbound consumers after pipeline construction but before start().
Both outbound rings start before inbound, or the engine would publish into rings with no running consumers. Teardown is the strict reverse (server stop, then drain inbound, snapshot, outbound), installed as a JVM shutdown hook with main parked on a CountDownLatch.
engine.setExecutionListener(handler) is the one line that fails silently if omitted: the listener defaults to NO_OP, so the server would accept and match orders while emitting no EXEC events at all, with no error surfaced.
Closes the deferred stale-Order bug by deletion rather than correction: the new Main never constructs an Order. Orders arrive over WebSocket and the Order is built inside MatchingEngineHandler.process() from the OrderEvent, where domain validation fires. Constructing orders in Main would also have violated the single-writer principle, since only the inbound consumer thread may mutate the book. For the same reason there is no book seeding — an empty book at bring-up is correct.
Port defaults to 8080, overridable as args[0]. Startup logs the endpoint and copy-pasteable NEW/CANCEL JSON samples.
Smoke test passed: resting BUY 10 @ 15000 -> EXEC/ORDER_ACCEPTED + BOOK (bestBid 15000, bids [[15000,10]]); crossing SELL 4 @ 15000 -> EXEC/ORDER_FILLED (tradeId 1, price 15000 passive, aggressor 2, passive 1) + BOOK reduced to [[15000,6]]. Confirms JSON -> JsonToFix -> FixParser -> inbound ring -> engine -> both outbound rings -> JSON -> wire.
Note for Phase 5: EXEC and BOOK are independent consumers with separate sequence counters, so their relative arrival order is not guaranteed — this was observed in the smoke test. The React client must treat BOOK as authoritative state and EXEC as notification.
Also updates Build_Guide_Phase4.md: P4-7 ✅ with as-built notes, P4-8 🔜.

test(net): WebSocket round-trip integration test — closes Phase 4 (P4-8)
The SRS §6.2 round-trip proven over real sockets: a real Netty WS client connects to the fully assembled server on an ephemeral port, submits orders as JSON, and asserts the EXEC/BOOK JSON pushed back.
WebSocketRoundTripTest assembles the whole pipeline in @BeforeEach, replicating Main's load-bearing wiring order verbatim (engine -> outbound + snapshot pipelines -> MatchingEngineHandler -> setExecutionListener -> inbound pipeline -> OrderGateway -> WebSocketServer(0) -> WebSocketPublisher -> register roles -> start). Test-local fixture rather than a Main refactor, since Main parks on a CountDownLatch behind a shutdown hook and isn't programmatically reusable.
Two properties of the running system shape the test:
- EXEC and BOOK are independent consumers with separate sequence counters and interleave unpredictably. awaitFrame matches on a parsed predicate, removes matched frames so none is matched twice, and retains non-matching frames for later awaits (each stage asserts on both an EXEC and a BOOK). The expected book shape is folded into the predicate so a stale [[15000,10]] never satisfies a [[15000,6]] await. No assertion assumes "frame N is the fill". - Four-plus daemon-thread hops: every assertion is a bounded await (2s ceiling, fast path immediate); no Thread.sleep as a sync primitive. @BeforeEach gates on ChannelGroup size == 1 before running, so the first snapshot can't publish into an empty group and get dropped by the publisher's empty-group early-out.
Coverage: resting BUY -> ORDER_ACCEPTED + BOOK bid level; crossing SELL -> ORDER_FILLED at the passive price with correct aggressor/passive ids + BOOK reduced; CANCEL (OrigClOrdID) -> ORDER_CANCELLED (orderId = cancelled order id, verified against the handler's cancel branch) + empty book; and a negative - malformed JSON publishes nothing and the same connection still round-trips a valid order, proving the boundary drop kills neither the worker thread nor the channel.
Reuses P4-4's WebSocketServerTest loopback-client idiom (lifted into a private LoopbackClient with a text-frame sink and matchers); WebSocketServerTest is untouched. Both tests green.

Package-private clock ctor injects a fixed clock for deterministic tests - Sole inbound producer (single-writer, SRS §5.2): ProducerType.SINGLE, onFrame not thread-safe by design - Imports com.lmax (ring producer) but not io.netty; decoder->gateway adapter deferred to Phase 4 - Tests reuse the Step 6.5 CapturingOrderHandler over the real InboundPipeline: valid D/F reach the ring, corrupt-checksum and null frames are dropped, slot reuse shows no field bleed

feat(publisher): WebSocket fan-out publisher for execution and book-snapshot events (P4-6)
Add WebSocketPublisher as the outbound edge to React clients, bridging the two Disruptor consumer threads to the Netty ChannelGroup.
- WebSocketPublisher: two stored EventHandler fields (executionHandler / snapshotHandler) allocated once at construction via method-reference, never per message. onExecution emits EXEC frames; onSnapshot emits BOOK frames. Skips serialization entirely when the group is empty. - Serialization: integer cents only — price formatting is React's job (§4). EXEC carries execType name + all carrier fields. BOOK serializes ONLY the [0, levelCount) valid prefix of each side; poisoned array tails never reach the wire (count-authoritative reuse contract). - Slot discipline: each onEvent builds a fresh JSON String fully inside the call before the slot can advance; the mutable carrier is never retained. Fan-out via ChannelGroup is safe from the consumer thread — Netty marshals each write to the channel's own event loop. - ObjectMapper is thread-safe; the two handlers run on different Disruptor consumer threads with no shared mutable serialization scratch. - Tests (WebSocketPublisherTest): EXEC field mapping, NA=-1 sentinel, BOOK valid-prefix-only with poisoned tails, empty-book, one-sided book, ChannelGroup write path, two-channel fan-out with unique EmbeddedChannelId, empty-group skip, and slot-discipline (mutate slot after dispatch). All green.

P4-7: Main bring-up — full pipeline assembled and running
Rewrite Main as the real bootstrap, wiring the complete path from WebSocket client to matching engine and back out to all subscribers (SRS §7, guide P4-7).
Wiring order, which is load-bearing:
MatchingEngine -> OutboundPipeline + SnapshotPipeline (construct) -> MatchingEngineHandler(engine, execRing, snapshotRing) -> engine.setExecutionListener(handler) -> InboundPipeline(handler) -> OrderGateway(inboundRing) -> WebSocketServer(port, gateway) // owns the ChannelGroup -> WebSocketPublisher(server.getChannelGroup()) -> register EXEC/BOOK roles + TradeLogger + MarketDataService -> start outbound, snapshot, inbound, server
The construction graph is circular on paper: the publisher needs the ChannelGroup, which the server owns; the server needs the gateway; the gateway needs the inbound ring; and InboundPipeline attaches its consumer at construction, so the handler must pre-exist the pipeline. Resolved by building the server before the publisher — the group exists at construction, before start() — and registering outbound consumers after pipeline construction but before start().
Both outbound rings start before inbound, or the engine would publish into rings with no running consumers. Teardown is the strict reverse (server stop, then drain inbound, snapshot, outbound), installed as a JVM shutdown hook with main parked on a CountDownLatch.
engine.setExecutionListener(handler) is the one line that fails silently if omitted: the listener defaults to NO_OP, so the server would accept and match orders while emitting no EXEC events at all, with no error surfaced.
Closes the deferred stale-Order bug by deletion rather than correction: the new Main never constructs an Order. Orders arrive over WebSocket and the Order is built inside MatchingEngineHandler.process() from the OrderEvent, where domain validation fires. Constructing orders in Main would also have violated the single-writer principle, since only the inbound consumer thread may mutate the book. For the same reason there is no book seeding — an empty book at bring-up is correct.
Port defaults to 8080, overridable as args[0]. Startup logs the endpoint and copy-pasteable NEW/CANCEL JSON samples.
Smoke test passed: resting BUY 10 @ 15000 -> EXEC/ORDER_ACCEPTED + BOOK (bestBid 15000, bids [[15000,10]]); crossing SELL 4 @ 15000 -> EXEC/ORDER_FILLED (tradeId 1, price 15000 passive, aggressor 2, passive 1) + BOOK reduced to [[15000,6]]. Confirms JSON -> JsonToFix -> FixParser -> inbound ring -> engine -> both outbound rings -> JSON -> wire.
Note for Phase 5: EXEC and BOOK are independent consumers with separate sequence counters, so their relative arrival order is not guaranteed — this was observed in the smoke test. The React client must treat BOOK as authoritative state and EXEC as notification.
Also updates Build_Guide_Phase4.md: P4-7 ✅ with as-built notes, P4-8 .

test(net): WebSocket round-trip integration test — closes Phase 4 (P4-8)
The SRS §6.2 round-trip proven over real sockets: a real Netty WS client connects to the fully assembled server on an ephemeral port, submits orders as JSON, and asserts the EXEC/BOOK JSON pushed back.
WebSocketRoundTripTest assembles the whole pipeline in @BeforeEach, replicating Main's load-bearing wiring order verbatim (engine -> outbound + snapshot pipelines -> MatchingEngineHandler -> setExecutionListener -> inbound pipeline -> OrderGateway -> WebSocketServer(0) -> WebSocketPublisher -> register roles -> start). Test-local fixture rather than a Main refactor, since Main parks on a CountDownLatch behind a shutdown hook and isn't programmatically reusable.
Two properties of the running system shape the test:
- EXEC and BOOK are independent consumers with separate sequence counters and interleave unpredictably. awaitFrame matches on a parsed predicate, removes matched frames so none is matched twice, and retains non-matching frames for later awaits (each stage asserts on both an EXEC and a BOOK). The expected book shape is folded into the predicate so a stale [[15000,10]] never satisfies a [[15000,6]] await. No assertion assumes "frame N is the fill". - Four-plus daemon-thread hops: every assertion is a bounded await (2s ceiling, fast path immediate); no Thread.sleep as a sync primitive. @BeforeEach gates on ChannelGroup size == 1 before running, so the first snapshot can't publish into an empty group and get dropped by the publisher's empty-group early-out.
Coverage: resting BUY -> ORDER_ACCEPTED + BOOK bid level; crossing SELL -> ORDER_FILLED at the passive price with correct aggressor/passive ids + BOOK reduced; CANCEL (OrigClOrdID) -> ORDER_CANCELLED (orderId = cancelled order id, verified against the handler's cancel branch) + empty book; and a negative - malformed JSON publishes nothing and the same connection still round-trips a valid order, proving the boundary drop kills neither the worker thread nor the channel.
Reuses P4-4's WebSocketServerTest loopback-client idiom (lifted into a private LoopbackClient with a text-frame sink and matchers); WebSocketServerTest is untouched. Both tests green.
